translations.source_sense_description: сделать более мягким, уменьшить жёсткость, твёрдость

glosses: To make something soft or softer.

examples.text: Soften the butter before beating in the sugar.

glosses: To undermine the morale of someone (often soften up).

examples.text: Before the invasion, we softened up the enemy with the artillery.

glosses: To make less harsh

examples.text: Having second thoughts, I softened my criticism.
I have recently reclad the south-west facing side of my single-storey cottage […]. I now want to plant some climbers of more manageable proportions to soften the building.

glosses: To become soft or softer

examples.text: The butter softened as it warmed up.

glosses: To become or make (a consonant) more lenis, to lenite.
To palatalize.

translations.source_sense_description: сделать менее суровым, строгим, жестоким, вызвать чувство доброты, мягкости

glosses: To ease a burden, particularly to ease a worry; make less painful; to comfort.

examples.text: All that charity can do where injustice exists is here and there to somewhat mollify the effects of injustice.
The draft Charter School Handbook issued in November 1994 sought to mollify concerns over teacher quality, if not ATA membership, by requiring teacher certification.

glosses: To appease anger, pacify, gain the good will of.

examples.text: Although this invitation was accompanied with a curtsey that might have softened the heart of a church-warden, it by no means mollified the beadle.
The angry goat was quite mollified by the respectful tone in which he was addressed.
There were no honeyed words from Dr. Beeching to mollify Scottish feeling on rail service closures during his one-day visit in May.

But these answers did not mollify Grassley. Specifically, he objected to Abedin’s becoming an S.G.E., because he believed she provided no irreplaceable expertise and therefore her designation as one had violated Congress’s intent when it created the program, in 1962.

Earlier this year, amid the challenge to the public charge rule arising from the Covid-19 virus, Chief Justice John Roberts took the lead against immigrant interests yet mollified liberals poised to dissent publicly, CNN’s Joan Biskupic reported this week.

glosses: To soften; to make tender.

examples.text: Nor is it any more difficulty for him to mollifie what is hard, then it is to harden what is so soft and fluid as the Aire.
By thy kindness thou wilt melt and mollify his spirit towards thee, as hardest metals are melted by coals of fire …

translations.source_sense_description: сделать менее сильным и резким; ослабить, умерить

glosses: Lack of difficulty; the ability to do something easily.

examples.text: He played the ukelele with ease.
The ease of lifting the weight, despite lack of skill, came from her pure strength.
Her young boy lifted a weight with ease too, as that one wasn't too heavy
The ease with which she passed all the exams surprised her.

glosses: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness
Freedom from pain, hardship, and annoyance, sometimes (derogatory, archaic) idleness, sloth.

examples.text: She enjoyed the ease of living in a house where the servants did all the work.

glosses: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness
Freedom from worry and concern; peace; sometimes (derogatory, archaic) indifference.

examples.text: The pension set her mind at ease.
There is ease in the soul of Slid and there be calms upon the sea; also, there be storms upon the sea and troubles in the soul of Slid, for the gods have many moods.

glosses: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness
Freedom from effort; leisure, rest.

examples.text: We took our ease on the patio.

glosses: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness
Freedom from financial effort or worry; affluence.

examples.text: His inheritance catapulted him into a life of ease.

glosses: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness
Freedom from embarrassment or awkwardness; grace.

examples.text: She dealt with the faculty with combined authority and ease.

glosses: Relief, an end to discomfort
Followed by of or from: release from or reduction of pain, hardship, or annoyance.

examples.text: Take one pill every 12 hours to provide ease from pain.

glosses: Relief, an end to discomfort
Release from intestinal discomfort: defecation.
Relief, an end to discomfort
Release from constraint, obligation, or a constrained position.

examples.text: At ease, soldier!

glosses: Relief, an end to discomfort
Additional space provided to allow greater movement.

examples.text: Add some ease to the waist measurement.

glosses: A convenience; a luxury.
A relief; an easement.
To free (something) from pain, worry, agitation, etc.

examples.text: He eased his conscience by confessing.

And ſure, although it was invented to eaſe his mynde of griefe, there be a number of caveats therein to forewarne other young gentlemen to foreſtand with good government their folowing yl fortunes; […]

Elyse Saugstad, a professional skier, wore a backpack equipped with an air bag, a relatively new and expensive part of the arsenal that backcountry users increasingly carry to ease their minds and increase survival odds in case of an avalanche.

glosses: To alleviate, assuage or lessen (pain).

examples.text: He loosened his shoe to ease the pain.
His words of comfort eased his friend's pain and distress.

glosses: To give respite to (someone).

examples.text: The provision of extra staff eased their workload.
An extra rush-hour train has eased overcrowding of the former 5.39 p.m. to Salisbury; this now leaves at 5.43 and an additional electric service to Alton departs at 5.39 p.m.

glosses: To loosen or slacken the tension on a line.

examples.text: We eased the boom vang, then lowered the sail.

glosses: To reduce the difficulty of (something).

examples.text: We had to ease the entry requirements.
I want to thank you all for easing my coming out.

glosses: To move (something) slowly and carefully.

examples.text: He eased the cork from the bottle.
Ease down off boulders; a jump may jar or sprain.
Giant oil-tankers can often be seen easing up and down Milford Haven, where a vast new port has been developed since the late 1950s.

glosses: To lessen in intensity.

examples.text: The pain eased overnight.

glosses: To proceed with little effort.

examples.text: The car eased onto the motorway.
"There's no other traffic on this line. We are 20 minutes ahead of time, so I'm easing back," says Waddicor as he approaches the crossing of HS2.

glosses: To take something from (a person), especially by robbery.

examples.text: Coming up to the thief they eased him of his late acquisitions, which Redmond, restoring to the right owner, bound him over to prosecute the robber at the next assizes.
So I tucked my violin under my arm, and sallied out after the old budgy ragman, determined to ease him of his load at the very first lonesome corner I could track him to.

translations.source_sense_description: сделать менее сильным и резким; ослабить, умерить

glosses: Not excessive; acting in moderation

examples.text: moderate language
a moderate Calvinist
travelling at a moderate speed
A number of moderate members managed […] to obtain a majority in a thin house.

glosses: more than mild, less than severe
Mediocre
Average priced; standard-deal
Not violent or rigorous; temperate; mild; gentle.

examples.text: a moderate winter
These are called the Islands of the Blest; rains fall there seldom, and in moderate showers, but for the most part they have gentle breezes, bringing along with them soft dews

glosses: Having an intermediate position between liberal and conservative.
One who holds an intermediate position between extremes, as in politics.

examples.text: While the moderates usually propose political compromise, it's often only achieved when the extremists allow them so
The moderates are the natural advocates of ecumenism against the fanatics of their churches.

On the other side, RMT General Secretary Mick Lynch (a moderate) has to contend with the hardliners on his executive, whose intentions go way beyond trying to sort out their members' terms and conditions.

glosses: One of a party in Scottish Church history dominant in the 18th century, lax in doctrine and discipline, but intolerant of evangelicalism and popular rights. It caused the secessions of 1733 and 1761, and its final resultant was the Disruption of 1843.
To reduce the excessiveness of (something).

examples.text: to moderate rage, action, desires, etc.
By its astringent Quality, it moderates the relaxing quality of warm Water.

This leaves two strategies to increase the current in a positron beam. First is to provide a stronger positron source and second is to develop a more efficient method to moderate the source positrons into a monoenergetic beam.

glosses: To become less excessive.

examples.text: He used to be an extremist but moderated later in life.

glosses: To preside over (something) as a moderator.

examples.text: to moderate a synod

glosses: To act as a moderator; to assist in bringing to compromise.

examples.text: In the comment section, the moderator was moderating.

glosses: To supply with a moderator (substance that decreases the speed of neutrons in a nuclear reactor and hence increases likelihood of fission).

examples.text: a graphite-moderated reactor

translations.source_sense_description: сделать менее сильным и резким; ослабить, умерить

glosses: To make quiet or put at rest; to pacify or appease; to quell; to calm.

examples.text: to allay popular excitement
to allay the tumult of the passions
O love, be moderate, allay thy ecstacy, […]
They were forced to try to allay discontent by palliative measures.
He had to pretend to be drunk in order to allay the suspicions which might have been aroused by his appearance at the gate.
Kissinger was obviously doing his best to allay our government's growing apprehension in connection with Nixon's forthcoming trip to Peking.

glosses: To alleviate; to abate; to mitigate.

examples.text: to allay the severity of affliction or the bitterness of adversity

glosses: To subside, abate, become peaceful.

examples.text: And the wynde alayed, and there folowed a greate calme: and he sayde unto them: why are ye fearfull?

For raging wind blows up incessant showers,
And when the rage allays the rain begins.

glosses: To mix (metals); to mix with a baser metal; to alloy; to deteriorate.
To make worse by the introduction of inferior elements.

examples.text: Yet far be it from us to condemn all their works to be dross, because debased and allayed with superstitious intents […]

glosses: Alleviation; abatement; check.
An alloy.

translations.source_sense_description: сделать менее сильным и резким; ослабить, умерить

glosses: To reduce or lessen the severity of a pain or difficulty.

examples.text: alleviate his pain
Alcohol is often a cheap tool to alleviate the stress of a hard day.

glosses: (finance) to pay down partially.

examples.text: There are different ways to alleviate your financial debt.
